finding.why: Group 9's only test wraps fetchPage in try { on FirestorePermissionDeniedException: pass; on Exception: pass; falls through with no throw: also pass }. All three possible outcomes are treated as success, so the test cannot fail no matter what _guardPermission does. Repo-wide grep confirms no other test anywhere constructs a raw FirebaseException(code:'permission-denied') to exercise this conversion — every other site (sync_orchestrator_test.dart, sy3_sync_error_message_sanitize_test.dart) injects FirestorePermissionDeniedException directly, bypassing the conversion entirely. Yet sync_orchestrator.dart, pull_pipeline.dart (x2), and tutored_pull_service.dart all branch on the resulting typed exception — a broken e.code=='permission-denied' mapping (e.g. an SDK error-code rename) would silently degrade permission-denied handling everywhere downstream while CI stays green.
finding.recommendation: Replace the strict-rules/try-catch-all test with a mocktail interaction mock or hand-rolled fake CollectionReference/Query whose .get() throws a real FirebaseException(plugin:'cloud_firestore', code:'permission-denied'), and assert fetchPage rethrows FirestorePermissionDeniedException specifically (no alternate silently-passing branch).
acceptance_criteria: New/updated test constructs FirebaseException(code:'permission-denied') via a mock and asserts throwsA(isA<FirestorePermissionDeniedException>()) with no catch-all pass branch
